name: git-guardrails
description: Git-level guardrails for local repos via core.hooksPath: a reference-transaction hook that aborts ref updates before they land - branch names must match fix|feat|chore|docs (R1), a cap on parallel local branches (R2, guardrails.maxBranches, default 1), commits on a branch with no upstream rejected until 'git push -u origin <branch>' (R3), and no direct commits to the default branch - only fast-forwards to what origin already has (R4). Default branch resolution falls back origin/HEAD symref -> refs/remotes/origin/main -> refs/remotes/origin/master -> local main -> local master, because a fresh clone of an empty remote has no refs/remotes/origin/HEAD. Deletions and all non-refs/heads namespaces always pass, repos without origin only get R1+R2, and internal errors fail closed with a report link and no bypass hint. guardrails.maxBranches is read from the user-global config only, so a repo cannot relax its own limit; GIT_QUARANTINE_PATH is never a bypass. Only bare receive-sides are exempt. Every standard hook name (pre-commit, commit-msg, prepare-commit-msg, pre-push, post-checkout, post-merge, pre-rebase, post-rewrite) chains to the repo's own hook in $(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/hooks so existing husky/lefthook/pre-commit setups keep working. Claude Code side: hooks/hooks.json wires a PreToolUse gate on Bash that denies anything that would switch the guardrails off or dodge them (writing core.hooksPath or guardrails.*, exporting GIT_QUARANTINE_PATH, --no-verify, any force push including +-refspecs and --mirror, git branch -D, git push --delete, git worktree add outside <repo>/.worktrees), and a Stop hook that blocks once on unpushed commits and honours stop_hook_active so it never loops; the gate fails closed and never prints 'allow', so normal permission prompts stay intact. bin/install-git-guardrails: dry run by default, --apply copies git-hooks/ to the stable path ~/.config/git-guardrails/hooks and sets global core.hooksPath (refuses a foreign hooksPath without --force), --uninstall unsets it only when it points at that dir and never deletes the files; the dry run also scans given roots (default ~/Documents) and names every repo whose repo-local core.hooksPath would shadow the global install, or that has its own .git/hooks/reference-transaction. Ships bin/git-tidy: branch/worktree table with upstream, ahead/behind, merged-into-default and prunable worktrees, dry-run by default, --prune deletes only provably safe branches (never the default, never the current, never force). Python 3 stdlib plus POSIX sh shims; sandbox-tested against a local bare remote in mktemp with GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL isolated.
